guide.summary: OpenProject documents OAuth2 authorization code flow for its API v3 on each instance. Confidential apps select scopes, and api_v3 is the default and standard API scope. The documented collection endpoint GET /api/v3/work_packages returns work packages with offset and pageSize pagination. Results follow the connected person's access. Each customer instance needs an OAuth application registered by an administrator, and the instance base URL remains a user input. Setup and execution remain untested.

findings.title: Authorization code flow with a confidential OAuth application on the customer instance
findings.detail: The admin creates an OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications and notes the Client ID and secret. The authorization code flow then uses the instance's /oauth/authorize and /oauth/token endpoints. Tokens are bearer tokens used on behalf of the current user.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer-owned OpenProject instance with developer-owned OAuth for customer accounts

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.
With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.

findings.title: api_v3 scope grants the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope. It is the default when no scope is checked, and it is the documented grant covering the work packages list endpoint. It is broad across the standard API, so the app must enforce read-only use itself and must not call write endpoints.
findings.appliesWhen: Read-only work package title retrieval through the standard API

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Connected person must have access to the work packages
findings.detail: Results depend on the connected person's existing account access. The workspace-scoped error says the user cannot see work packages of a project without permission. Test with a representative account that has access before relying on the results.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their own accounts on their instances

findings.title: Access tokens expire after two hours by default
findings.detail: The documented default bearer token lifetime is two hours. Without refresh, API requests return an error and a new token must be requested. The response also includes a refresh token.

evidence.quote: Please note that your Bearer token will expire after two hours (default) and you will have to click on “Request Token” again. Otherwise your API request will return an error

steps.title: Register a confidential OAuth application on the customer instance
steps.detail: An OpenProject administrator on the customer instance creates an OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications, selects the api_v3 scope, marks it Confidential, and records the Client ID and Client secret. Use a redirect URL provided by the developer's client application.
steps.doneWhen: The OAuth application exists with api_v3 scope, a confidential type, and a noted Client ID and Client secret; no credentials are stored in code.

steps.title: Prepare the developer app to start the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Configure the developer application with the instance's authorization and token endpoints, the registered Client ID and secret, the redirect URI, and scope api_v3. Do not run the authorization or token exchange in this step.

evidence.quote: OAuth endpoints The authentication endpoints of OpenProject OAuth2 server are:
Auth URL: https://example.com/oauth/authorize Access Token URL: https://example.com/oauth/token

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer-provided full HTTPS URL
CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET: from the registered application

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for a bearer token
steps.detail: Before exchanging the code, the connected person must authorize access by visiting the authorize URL with response_type=code, client_id=<CLIENT_ID>, redirect_uri=<REDIRECT_URI> and scope=api_v3 (only api_v3 is needed; the scope must be a list separated by %20 if multiple). Consent returns a code in the redirect. Then POST to the token endpoint with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, code and redirect_uri; the response contains access_token and a refresh_token. This is an unexecuted authorization step; no request has been run.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in and a refresh_token, and the authorize step returned a code.

steps.title: Read the first page of work packages the connected person can access
steps.detail: Call the documented work packages collection with a bearer token and pageSize. Only read titles from the subject property. Expected output is a HAL collection with _embedded.elements, total and nextByOffset when more pages exist.
steps.doneWhen: The response is HTTP 200 with a collection whose elements contain subject values, and total and count are present. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.doneWhen: Only GET requests appear in the outgoing request log and the grant shows the api_v3 scope.

steps.title: Read the next page of work packages using offset pagination
steps.detail: Repeat the collection request with the next offset value from the prior response until the total count is reached. Follow nextByOffset from the prior response by resolving its relative href against the same HTTPS instance host. The end condition is when count plus offset-based position covers total.
steps.doneWhen: Subsequent pages return HTTP 200 and the full set of elements up to total has been read. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
